liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Big Railroad Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer says an interview with Dick recommended the Other One into Big Railroad Blues stretch; reviewer also enjoyed Cryptical Envelopment; Reviewer says Big Railroad Blues storms out of Cryptical Envelopment, despite not usually liking the song [8][16]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer calls Jack Straw a good gauge of a show; this one is played tightly together, and Tennessee Jed and El Paso follow [9]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer praises Phil's tone and Keith's inspired playing, though his piano still sounds a bit honky-tonk for this song [12]

## The recordings

- **gd71-11-12.sbd.clugston.4759.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 129 min; rated 4.55/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording very quiet and compressed, with vocals that seem to lack high-end frequencies; Reviewer hears a fairly quiet show with slight hiss, and keyboards sitting further forward than usual [7][13]
- **gd1971-11-12.sbd.lai.3347.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 129 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Mix is pretty good when audio works, but this copy has too many dropouts for downloading; First disc has severe left-channel dropouts, from under a second to nearly two minutes, with scratchy static; Uploader calls it one of the best-balanced early Keith shows, with a bright, full piano [2][14]
- **gd1971-11-12.sbd-set2.miller.14916.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 66 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: Keith's piano sits quite high in the mix in the earlier tracks of this set [16]
- **gd1971-11-12.137396.sbd.miller.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 130 min; rated 0.5/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls radio reports of cancellation, then reversal; start moved from 8 to 10 PM because band's equipment hadn't arrived by plane [11]
- New Riders began around 11 PM, and Jerry played with them [11]
- Keith is introduced at one point; Pigpen was very sick and stayed home [13]
- Reviewer hadn't heard 1971 shows in a while and finds this night full of young, raw energy [10]
- Reviewer thinks the fall 1971 Texas run is underrated, with energetic shows and impressively strong playing from newcomer Keith [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-11-12.sbd.clugston.4759.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Master soundboard reel transferred to cassette, then DAT, then CDR [1]
- **gd1971-11-12.sbd-set2.miller.14916.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller and Alan Fink; source: S : MC > C > SONIC SOLUTIONS > CDR > EAC > COOL EDIT PRO > SHN [5]. Also: Second set edited by Alan J Fink in Cool Edit Pro; two gaps patched from another soundboard source [5]
- **gd1971-11-12.137396.sbd.miller.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: Source: Sbd > master reel (vault) > reel (dick latvala) > dat 48k (rob Eaton); Transfer: Dat > Sony R500 > Sound Devices 744T > wav 16/48; transfer by Charlie… [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [current-page:url:arg:3 | Grateful Dead](https://www.dead.net/tags/san-antonio-civic-auditorium) [20]
